clue.text: Fence in the bird?

parts.note: read whimsically, a barrier rail set up on dry ground would be a fence on the land; the question mark flags that this fanciful split also names a marsh bird, the corncrake

explanation.walkthrough: The bird is the corncrake; split in two, its name looks like a rail (fence) on land.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a bird of the rail family also known by this name.

clue.text: Opposed to Turkish leader in a way

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish chief or commander
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone stands against an Ottoman ruler's methods.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is an Ottoman title for a commander; ST (street) is a standard crossword 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set in opposition to something is the plain sense of this preposition.

clue.text: Is music hall sure to go bust? That's the talk

parts.note: a disco is a hall where music is played for dancing

indicators.note: going bust means breaking apart, so the letters of sure are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a variety theatre is bound to fail, calling it mere chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go bust' scrambles SURE into URSE after DISCO; 'Is' simply opens the question and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a spoken or written discussion, a talk on a subject.

clue.text: Prevents victory in verse drama for example

indicators.note: the word in tells us the victory letters go inside the arts word

parts.note: verse and drama are examples of the arts
VE stands for victory in Europe, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A triumph in poetic theatre stops something happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts VE (Victory in Europe, as in VE Day of 1945) inside ARTS, which verse and drama exemplify.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to ward it off, preventing it.

clue.text: Musical inheritance of the Welsh ?

parts.note: points to the song passed down to the people of Wales from their forebears, their national anthem

explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh national anthem is 'Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau', known in English by this title, an inheritance in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The national anthem of Wales celebrates the country handed down by previous generations.

clue.text: Perceiving Desmond's left in tears-such a shame!

indicators.note: left here means left off, so the short name is dropped from the front of the longer word

parts.note: to descry is to catch sight of, perceive
Des is short for Desmond

explanation.surface: Someone sees that a friend has gone and weeps at the pity of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops DES from DESCRYING; the closing 'such a shame' nods to the phrase 'a crying shame'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weeping with tears running down is said to be sobbing in this way.

clue.text: Mythical horsemen

parts.note: creatures of Greek legend that are half man, half horse

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these beings have a human torso on a horse's body, literally horse-men.

clue.text: Takes the air in his lane, for a change

indicators.note: a change of order means the letters of his and lane are shuffled into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone breathes deeply on a country path, enjoying a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' sounds like a stroll for variety but rearranges HIS LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing breath into the lungs is taking in air.

clue.text: Speedwell, "foreign version of the English equivalent

parts.note: German is a foreign language to the English
der is the German version of the English word the

explanation.surface: A flower name seems to be a translation of an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts read as 'German der', the German for 'the'; the plant is the germander speedwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander speedwell is a common blue-flowered Veronica, so the first word names the plant.

clue.text: Scratch figure to discern fire-worshipper

parts.note: in golf a scratch player is expected to score par
to discern is to see

explanation.surface: A golfer's handicap number helps identify a follower of a fire cult.
explanation.walkthrough: A scratch golfer has no handicap, so their target is PAR. Parsees are Zoroastrians, often called fire-worshippers for their sacred fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsees are Indian Zoroastrians, whose temples keep a sacred flame burning.

clue.text: Lily shows up Ann, her replacement

indicators.note: replacing the letters in new positions means up, Ann and her are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called Lily outdoes Ann, who is taking her place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' shuffles UP ANN HER; 'shows' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nenuphar is an old name for the water lily.

clue.text: Several alternative figures

definitions.meaning: two numbers offered as alternatives, joined by the word or

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a few, and literally it is two numbers given as alternatives.

clue.text: Literally from start to finish a meadow plant

parts.note: from start to finish of the alphabet, taken literally as letters, is A to Z
lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A field flower runs from one end of a meadow to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From A to Z' means from start to finish, so taken literally the letters are A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub of the rhododendron family.

clue.text: Sailor on board takes the lead

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts the sailor between the two letters of the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the ship a sailor is aboard
tar is a familiar term for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman on deck assumes command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention for going inside SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who plays the main role in a film is said to have top billing in it.

clue.text: Science defied by word master Humpty-Dumpty

definitions.text: Science defied by word master Humpty-Dumpty

parts.words: Science defied by word master Humpty-Dumpty
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass Humpty Dumpty says a word means just what he chooses, flouting the study of meaning

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's Humpty Dumpty insists words mean whatever he wants, defying the discipline that studies meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of linguistics studies the meanings of words and sentences.

clue.text: Deeply affected, when forced into service

definitions.meaning: strongly moved or struck by something
pressed men were forced into the navy by press gangs

explanation.definitionFit: The word means much moved, and also describes sailors seized by the press gang for naval duty.

clue.text: Superficial injury from speeding

definitions.meaning: a surface burn or singeing of the skin

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes singeing on the surface and, informally, going extremely fast.

clue.text: Deeds of cartographers?

definitions.meaning: formal documents granting rights or privileges
people who chart, that is, mapmakers

explanation.definitionFit: Royal grants of rights are such documents, and the word also fancifully names mapmakers who chart.

clue.text: Move temporary substitute

definitions.meaning: to shift oneself, make a move
something improvised to serve for now

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means to shift; as one it is a stopgap arrangement.

clue.text: Girl cheated in US kind of cricket

parts.note: Katy is a girl's name
did someone means cheated them

explanation.surface: A young woman was swindled in an American cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' suggests the sport, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The katydid is a North American bush cricket named for its call.

clue.text: Sole ferry port

definitions.meaning: the Kent harbour with cross-Channel ferries to France

explanation.definitionFit: The fish is named after the Kent harbour, which is England's main Channel crossing point.

clue.text: Seat on board 'as safeguard for pilots

definitions.text: Seat on board 'as safeguard for pilots

parts.words: Seat on board 'as safeguard for pilots
parts.note: describes the seat in a military jet that fires the pilot clear of a stricken aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints ELECTOR, but the clue clearly means the ejector seat, and the differing letter is unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejection seat catapults aircrew out of a failing aircraft so they can parachute down.

clue.text: Three articles required by a girl

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl needs three items to complete her outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: AN, THE and A are the three grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female given name.

clue.text: Such garments to capture a girl !

parts.note: to net is to catch
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone suggests using underwear to trap a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nether garments' is a jocular old term for trousers or underwear, so the adjective fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower, and nether garments are those worn on the lower body.

clue.text: Neil's cut out the vestments

indicators.note: out signals the letters are set out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Neil has cut out the robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NEILS CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunicle is a short liturgical tunic worn by a subdeacon or bishop.

clue.text: In many, one hereditary element reveals the native

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
I is the Roman numeral one
a gene is the unit of heredity

explanation.surface: Among many, one inherited trait shows who belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: D (500) for 'many' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigene is a person born in a place, an aboriginal inhabitant.

clue.text: Raises for landlords who take one in

indicators.note: to take someone in is to house them, so the landlords hold the one letter
in completes the phrase take in, putting the single letter inside the landlords word

parts.note: hosts receive guests, as landlords of inns do
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Innkeepers get pay rises when they take in a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... in' puts I inside HOSTS. 'Raises' looks like a noun about pay; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to lift it up.

clue.text: I'd be in less trouble making edges

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so I'd and less are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reckons they'd be in less difficulty by being cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ID LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move sideways, furtively, inching along.

clue.text: Horse complaint of EXmoor huntsmen?

definitions.meaning: a disease of horses causing staggering
jokingly, those who hunt stags, as on Exmoor

explanation.walkthrough: Exmoor in south-west England is known for its stag hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease makes horses reel, and the word playfully names stag hunters.
